definitions.definition: The science of the lights in three branches — computation (gaṇita/siddhānta), horoscopy (horā) and mundane omens (saṃhitā) — of which the horā is called best; the 'eye of the Veda' (BS 1.9; BPHS 1.1–6).

cross_language.note: 'star-calculation', the Indian-derived astral science (translation, not a loan)
astrology as listed among the 'low arts' in DN 1; narrower than jyotiṣa

definitions.definition: The computational branch: treatises giving time-units, the yugas and kalpa, planetary revolutions, true positions, eclipses and the sphere; also called gaṇita or tantra (BS 1.9; SS).
The branch of mundane astrology and omens — courses of planets and comets, rain, portents, signs of persons, animals, sites and gems, augury — as in the Bṛhat Saṃhitā (BS 1.9; 2.17).

(1) Horoscopy, the branch revealing the ripening of karma of former births; the word is said to come from aho-rātra by dropping first and last syllables (BJ 1.3). (2) Half of a sign, ruled by the Sun or Moon (BJ 1.11). (3) A planetary hour.

notes: Scholarly account: from Greek hōra.

definitions.definition: A nativity or birth-horoscope, and the genre of horā texts on it (Bṛhajjātaka, Laghujātaka, Jātakapārijāta); distinct from the Buddhist Jātaka birth-stories.
Answering a question from the chart of the moment it is asked, together with the omens then present (Ṣaṭpañcāśikā; Praśna Mārga).
In Kerala the query is an elaborate rite (aṣṭamaṅgala-praśna, devaprāśna) diagnosing afflictions from curses and spirits and prescribing remedies (Praśna Mārga).

(1) A thirtieth of a day-and-night (48 minutes). (2) An auspicious moment chosen by tithi, weekday, asterism, yoga, karaṇa and rising sign for an undertaking — the subject of the muhūrta texts (Muhūrtacintāmaṇi).

A sign or omen from which future good or ill is inferred — celestial, atmospheric, terrestrial, bodily, dream, sound; for the Jains the eight 'great omens' (aṣṭāṅga-mahānimitta) are a science a monk must not live by.

cross_language.note: in DN 1.21 among the low arts (reading of signs)

definitions.definition: A portent: 'a change of nature' — produced by the gods' displeasure at men's misconduct, it announces coming calamity and is to be countered by pacification (BS 45.1–3); heavenly, atmospheric or earthly.

cross_language.note: among the low arts in DN 1.21

definitions.definition: Augury from birds and animals — their cries, movements and directions (BS 85–95; Vasantarāja Śākuna).

The 'knower of fate': the astrologer, also sāṃvatsara, daivavid, gaṇaka or jyotiṣī; he must know the three branches and be of good conduct; the king and even forest-dwellers consult him (BS 2; BPHS 1.7–8).
The calculator-astronomer who computes positions and calendars; the lives of such are told in the Gaṇakataraṅgiṇī.

The 'Person of Time': the zodiac as a body whose limbs are the twelve signs from the head (Aries) to the feet (Pisces) (BJ 1.4), whose self is the Sun and mind the Moon (BJ 2.1); an ocean no non-seer can cross (BS 2.4).

equivalents.note: the cosmic Person whose limbs are the world (RV 10.90) — an analogy of form, not an identity the jyotiṣa texts assert

definitions.definition: In jyotiṣa, the foreign (Greek) teachers of horā — 'mlecchas among whom this science is well established, honoured like seers' (BS 2.14) — whose views Varāhamihira cites (BJ 7.1, 11.1, 12.1).
A 'seizer': the nine planets — Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, Rāhu, Ketu — which 'moving, grasp the asterisms' (BPHS 3.4); forms of Janārdana giving the fruits of karma (BPHS 2.3).
A sign: one of the twelve equal divisions of the zodiac beginning with Aries, each of nine asterism-quarters; the limbs of Kālapuruṣa; synonyms kṣetra, gṛha, ṛkṣa, bha, bhavana (BJ 1.4).

One of the twelve houses counted from the ascendant, each governing a domain of life — body, family and speech, siblings, mother and home, children and intellect, enemies and disease, spouse, longevity and death, fortune and dharma, action, gains, loss and liberation (BJ 1.15–18; BPHS 11).

notes: Homonym of bhāva 'emotion/state/being' in other traditions; id disambiguated.

definitions.definition: The ascendant: the sign (and degree) rising in the east at the moment of birth or of the query — 'the rising of the signs is the lagna; by it the results for the born are to be judged' (BPHS 3.6).
The angles: the 1st, 4th, 7th and 10th houses (kaṇṭaka, catuṣṭaya), where planets are strong (BJ 1.17).

notes: Scholarly account: from Greek kentron.

definitions.definition: The 5th and 9th houses (with the 1st), the most auspicious houses; lords of angles and trines together make royal yogas (BPHS 39).
The 6th, 8th and 12th houses — enemies and disease, death, loss — whose lords and occupants afflict.
The 'increasing' houses, 3rd, 6th, 10th and 11th, where malefics do good (BJ 1.15).
The succedent houses (2, 5, 8, 11) following the angles (BJ 1.18).

notes: Scholarly account: from Greek epanaphora.

definitions.definition: The cadent houses (3, 6, 9, 12) following the succedents (BJ 1.18).

notes: Scholarly account: from Greek apoklima.

definitions.definition: A 'killer': the lords of and planets in the 2nd and 7th houses (the houses of death reckoned from the 8th and 3rd), whose periods may bring death when longevity is ending (BPHS 44).
Exaltation: the sign and degree where a planet is most exalted — Sun Aries 10°, Moon Taurus 3°, Mars Capricorn 28°, Mercury Virgo 15°, Jupiter Cancer 5°, Venus Pisces 27°, Saturn Libra 20° (BJ 1.13).
Fall (debilitation): the seventh sign from a planet's exaltation (BJ 1.13); a fallen planet's cancellation (nīcabhaṅga) can itself give a royal yoga.

A planet's 'root-trine' sign, next in strength after exaltation: Sun Leo, Moon Taurus, Mars Aries, Mercury Virgo, Jupiter Sagittarius, Venus Libra, Saturn Aquarius (BJ 1.14 with commentaries; BPHS 3).
A planet or ascendant occupying the same sign in the birth chart and the navāṃśa — the first navāṃśa of movable, the middle of fixed and the last of dual signs — held to give good results (BJ 1.14).

A planet 'set' in the sun's rays; such a planet loses strength, and renunciation-planets set in the sun give devotion without initiation (BJ 15.2; BPHS 79.4); Jupiter or Venus set bars marriages and other rites.
Retrogression; a retrograde planet is counted strong for longevity (BJ 7.2) and is a name of Mars (BJ 2.2).
A planet's 'glance' at other houses: all aspect the 7th fully, and the 3rd/10th, 5th/9th and 4th/8th partially; Saturn, Jupiter and Mars aspect these respectively in full (BJ 2.13).

notes: Homonym of dṛṣṭi 'view' (Jain/Buddhist); id disambiguated.

definitions.definition: In the Jaimini system, aspect by signs: each sign aspects the sign facing it and those at its sides — movable signs the fixed (but the adjacent), fixed the movable (but the adjacent), dual signs one another (Jaimini 1.1.2–3; BPHS 8).

A division of each sign into equal parts, each ruled by a planet, forming a separate chart: six in Varāhamihira (sign, horā, drekkāṇa, navāṃśa, twelfth, thirtieth: BJ 1.9), sixteen in Parāśara (BPHS 6.2–4).
The ninth-part of a sign (3°20′), one asterism-quarter; its chart is the most used division after the birth chart (BJ 1.6; BPHS 6).
The third-part (decan) of a sign; its figures and the 22nd decan (reckoned for death) are described in BJ 27 and 25.11.

notes: Scholarly account: from Greek dekanos.

definitions.definition: The sixfold strength of a planet — positional, directional, temporal, motional, natural and aspectual — computed to judge its power to give results (BPHS 27).
The 'eightfold division': benefic points (bindu) contributed to each sign by the seven planets and the ascendant, used to judge transits and longevity (BJ 9; BPHS 66–72).

A planet signifying a person or matter: fixed natural significators (the Sun of the father and self, the Moon of the mother and mind…) and, in Jaimini and Parāśara, the variable significators (cara-kāraka) by degrees (BPHS 32).

notes: Homonym of the grammatical kāraka; id disambiguated.

definitions.definition: The significator of the self: the planet with the highest degrees in its sign among seven (or eight) (Jaimini 1.1.11; BPHS 32.3); called the king among the kārakas.
The navāṃśa sign occupied by the ātmakāraka, from which Jaimini judges dharma, the next world and liberation: Ketu in the twelfth from it gives kaivalya (Jaimini 1.2.13, 1.2.68–69; BPHS 33).

The 'mounted' image of a house: the sign as far from the house-lord as the lord is from the house; it shows how a matter appears in the world (BPHS 29; Jaimini); in Kerala praśna, the sign indicated by the querist.
The ārūḍha of the twelfth house, judged for marriage and spouse in the Jaimini system (BPHS 30).
'Bolt' or intervention: planets in the 2nd, 4th and 11th from a house or planet that influence it, obstructed by those in the 12th, 10th and 3rd (BPHS 31; Jaimini).
A planet that rules both an angle and a trine for a given ascendant (e.g. Saturn for Taurus and Libra), producing royal yoga by itself (BPHS 34; Laghupārāśarī).

A planetary period: the life divided into periods ruled in turn by planets or signs, with sub-periods (antardaśā/bhukti), in which each ruler gives its fruits; many systems are taught, the Viṃśottarī chief in the Kali age (BPHS 46.3–15).

(1) A combination of planets, signs and houses producing a definite result — royal, wealth, renunciation, nābhasa and others (BJ 11–15). (2) One of the 27 yogas of the almanac, from the sum of the longitudes of sun and moon.

notes: Homonym of yoga as discipline; id disambiguated.

definitions.definition: A combination making the native a king or like one — by exalted planets (BJ 11), or by the relation of angle- and trine-lords (BPHS 39); distinct from rājayoga as a path of meditation.
The combination for renunciation: four or more strong planets in one sign, the strongest deciding the order the native enters (BJ 15.1; BPHS 79.1–5).
'Elephant-lion' yoga: Jupiter in an angle from the Moon, giving fame and prosperity (later horā texts, e.g. Phaladīpikā 6).
A combination threatening early death or calamity, especially to infants (BJ 6), and its cancellation (ariṣṭa-bhaṅga) by benefic influences (BPHS 9–10).

The 'gift of life': methods of computing the length of life from the planets' positions — the rival methods of Maya, the Yavanas, Maṇittha, Parāśara, Jīvaśarman and Satya, of which Varāhamihira prefers Satya's (BJ 7).
The five-limbed almanac: lunar day (tithi), weekday (vāra), asterism (nakṣatra), yoga and karaṇa, by which the quality of any time is judged.
The lunar day: the time in which the moon gains 12° on the sun; thirty make a lunar month; each has a presiding deity and belongs to one of five classes (SS 1.13; MC 1.3–4).
The weekday, named for the planet ruling its first hour in the sequence Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn; each weekday suits certain classes of asterism and action (MC 1.4, 2.2–8).
Half a lunar day; eleven karaṇas — seven movable (Bava, Bālava, Kaulava, Taitila, Gara, Vaṇij, Viṣṭi) and four fixed (Śakuni, Catuṣpada, Nāga, Kiṃstughna); Viṣṭi (Bhadrā) is shunned (BS 99).

notes: Homonym of karaṇa 'instrument'; id disambiguated.

definitions.definition: The bright (śukla) and dark (kṛṣṇa) halves of the lunar month; the quality of tithis reverses between them (MC 1.4).

notes: Homonym of pakṣa 'thesis' in logic; id disambiguated.

definitions.definition: The reckoning of the lunar month as ending at new moon (usual in the south and west).
The reckoning of the lunar month as ending at full moon (usual in the north).
The intercalary lunar month in which no solar ingress occurs; also called mala-māsa, it is unfit for sacraments and many rites, though prized for devotion (Kālamādhava; Nirṇayasindhu).
A rare 'lost' lunar month containing two solar ingresses.
The sun's ingress into a sign, defining the solar month (SS 1.13); its time is a holy period (puṇyakāla) for bathing and gifts; Makara-saṃkrānti marks the northern course in the calendar.
The sun's southern course, the six months opposite to the uttarāyaṇa; in the Gītā part of the path of return (BhG 8.25).
A unit of 24 minutes, a sixtieth of a day; six prāṇas make a vināḍī and sixty vināḍīs a nāḍī (SS 1.11).
A complete revolution of a planet through the zodiac; the numbers of revolutions in a yuga or kalpa are the basic constants of a siddhānta (SS 1.29–34; Āryabhaṭīya 1.3).
The count of civil days elapsed from an epoch (the start of the kalpa or of the Kali age), from which mean positions are computed.

The arc between the moving equinox and the fixed starting point of the sidereal zodiac; the siddhāntas treat the solstitial points as oscillating (the Sūrya Siddhānta's libration of 27°), and schools differ on its value.
Reckoning longitudes from the moving equinox (tropical), used for the seasons and the sun's courses.
Reckoning longitudes from a fixed point among the stars (sidereal), the norm of the siddhāntas and of Indian horoscopy and almanacs.
A daily period of about an eighth of the daytime, falling at a different part of the day for each weekday, avoided for new undertakings (mainly South Indian practice).

notes: Classical textual basis not located; recorded as current practice.

definitions.definition: The seventh movable karaṇa, called Bhadrā, inauspicious for undertakings; BPHS has a pacification for births under it (BPHS 88).
The five asterisms from the second half of Dhaniṣṭhā to Revatī, during which certain acts — building roofs, gathering wood, southward journeys and cremation without special rites — are avoided.

notes: Rules from the muhūrta digests; exact sources not checked.

definitions.definition: The junctions of water and fire signs (Revatī–Aśvinī, Āśleṣā–Maghā, Jyeṣṭhā–Mūla) and of corresponding tithis and ascendants; birth there endangers the child or parents and requires pacification (BPHS 94).
The current movement of the planets counted from the natal Moon, 'generally used in practice': each planet is good in certain houses from the Moon and bad in others (BS 103.2–4).

notes: Homonym of gocara 'sense-field'; id disambiguated.

definitions.definition: The division of the land into nine regions like a tortoise, each ruled by three asterisms from Kṛttikā, by which omens are assigned to countries (BS 14.1).

A remedy that averts or lessens the evil shown in the chart: worship, mantra-recitation, fire-offering, gifts, vows, gems and pacification rites prescribed per planet or yoga (BPHS 84–96; Praśna Mārga).
In jyotiṣa, the pacification of planets, portents and inauspicious births by worship, oblation and gifts (BS 45.3–7; BPHS 84–96; YājñSm 1.295–308).

cross_language.note: a pacification rite listed among the low arts from which the Buddha abstains (DN 1.27)

definitions.definition: The sacrifice to the nine planets for prosperity, peace, rain, long life or nourishment, with their images, mantras, fuel-sticks and gifts (YājñSm 1.295–308; BPHS 84).
A gem: 'the fate that depends on gems is to be examined by experts', since good gems bring good to kings and bad ones harm (BS 79.1); later texts assign a gem to each planet to be worn as a remedy.
In jyotiṣa, prescribed gifts to brahmins that pacify an afflicting planet or portent — specific objects, colours and animals for each planet (YājñSm 1.295–306; BS 45.6).
In jyotiṣa, vows and fasts kept on the weekday or tithi of an afflicting planet or deity as part of the remedies (later horā and muhūrta practice).

In jyotiṣa, fate: karma, good and bad, produced in another birth, which yields birth in a good family and the like, and bears fruit together with human effort, as in farming (Yogayātrā 1.3–4); it is what the horā reveals (BJ 1.3).

In jyotiṣa, human effort: with fate it brings success, as effort and rain together bring a harvest (Yogayātrā 1.3–4); fate is human effort of a former body (YājñSm 1.349); a well-timed undertaking succeeds even with slight effort (BS 103.60).

In jyotiṣa (interpretive gloss): the karma 'earned in a former birth' whose ripening the horā reveals as a lamp reveals objects (BJ 1.3; LJ 1.3). The jyotiṣa texts say 'karma of a former birth'; the Vedāntic word prārabdha is applied by later practitioners.
The ripening of karma; a genre relating specific afflictions and inauspicious births to specific sins of former lives and prescribing expiations (Karmavipākasaṃhitā; BPHS 83).
The individual-soul portion present in every being alongside the supreme-Self portion; where it predominates the being is a jīva (BPHS 1.22; 2.8).
The supreme-Self portion present in all beings; it predominates in the planets, the gods' powers and the full avatāras (BPHS 1.22–24; 2.2–8).
The 'fault of Mars': Mars in certain houses (commonly the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th) of a marriage chart, held to endanger the spouse unless matched or cancelled.

notes: Widely applied in marriage matching; the classical verse usually quoted is of uncertain source.

definitions.definition: The 'seven and a half' years of Saturn's transit through the 12th, 1st and 2nd signs from the natal Moon, held to be a time of trials.

notes: Rests on the transit teaching (BS 103: Saturn good only in the 3rd, 6th and 11th from the Moon); the name is vernacular.

definitions.definition: The Perso-Arabic ('Tājik') system of annual and interrogational astrology in Sanskrit (Tājikanīlakaṇṭhī).
The annual chart cast for the sun's return to its natal longitude, with its own year-lord, muntha and sahamas (Tājikanīlakaṇṭhī, Varṣatantra).
The Tājika yoga of applying aspect, when a faster planet approaches exact aspect with a slower; the first and chief of the sixteen Tājika yogas.

notes: Scholarly account: from Arabic ittiṣāl.

definitions.definition: A sensitive point computed from three chart factors (like the Arabic 'lots'), e.g. the puṇya-sahama, used in Tājika.

notes: Scholarly account: from Arabic sahm.

definitions.definition: The Tājika progressed point advancing one sign per year from the natal ascendant.
A palm-leaf text which, the tradition holds, a seer wrote for a particular future consultant, found by thumb-impression and read in chapters (kāṇḍa).
The letter-numeral code (k, ṭ, p, y = 1 …) used to encode numbers in words — in the Jaimini Sūtras (signs, periods), in Kerala astronomy (candravākyas) and in many mnemonic verses.
Number-words: expressing numerals by objects of known count (e.g. veda = 4, rasa = 6, agni = 3), written from the lowest place, as in the siddhānta verses (SS 1.30).
Āryabhaṭa's system writing large numbers with consonants and vowels (ka = 1 … with vowels marking decimal places), used for the constants in the Gītikāpāda.

The name derived from the birth-asterism: the Vedāṅga Jyotiṣa says the knowers of the śāstra laid down a sacrificer's name from his nakṣatra (VJ r.28); later, each asterism-quarter is assigned a syllable for naming a child.

The 'site-man': a being who obstructed heaven and earth, pinned face-down by the gods who stay where they seized him, and made by the Creator into the god-filled figure laid over every site (BS 52.2–3).

In jyotiṣa, time is twofold: the time that ends the worlds, and reckonable time, gross (from the prāṇa) and subtle (from the truṭi) (SS 1.10–11); without beginning or end, it is inferred from the planets and stars (Āryabhaṭīya 3.11).

In the siddhāntas, the caturyuga of 4,320,000 solar years divided 4:3:2:1 into Kṛta, Tretā, Dvāpara and Kali following the feet of dharma (SS 1.15–17; BSS 1.7–9) — or, for Āryabhaṭa, into four equal quarters.
Twelve thousand divine years = 4,320,000 solar years, the unit in which revolutions are counted (SS 1.15; BSS 1.7).
In the siddhāntas, a day of Brahmā of 1,000 caturyugas with fourteen Manus and their junctions (SS 1.19–20); Āryabhaṭa counts 14 × 72 yugas (Āryabhaṭīya 1.5).
Seventy-one caturyugas with a closing junction of a Kṛta's length, a flood (SS 1.18).

The present, fourth age, whose beginning (3102 BCE by the siddhāntic epoch) is the zero of calendrical computation; Āryabhaṭa was 23 when 3600 of its years had passed (Āryabhaṭīya 3.10); in it the Viṃśottarī is the chief period-system (BPHS 46.14).

In jyotiṣa, (1) the first year of the Vedic five-year yuga (VJ; BS 8.24); (2) a year of the sixty-year Jupiter cycle beginning with Prabhava (BS 8.27–29); (3) 'sāṃvatsara' also names the astrologer (BS 2).

In horā and muhūrta, one of the 27 lunar mansions of 13°20′ (with Abhijit as 28th in muhūrta), each with a deity, a Viṃśottarī lord and a class of suitable actions (BS 97; MC 2.1–8); in the siddhāntas, the Lord's own twenty-sevenfold division (SS 12.25).

In jyotiṣa, the sun's northern course; Vedāṅga Jyotiṣa places the northward turning of sun and moon at the beginning of Śraviṣṭhā in Māgha (VJ r.6); in later calendars it is marked by Makara-saṃkrānti.

In horā, the liberation whose signs appear in the chart: Jupiter exalted in the 6th, an angle or the 8th, or the 12th rising in a benefic navāṃśa with the other planets weak (BJ 25.15); Ketu in the 12th from the kārakāṃśa gives kaivalya (Jaimini 1.2.69).
In the Jaimini system, the liberation indicated by the kārakāṃśa exalted, or by Ketu in the twelfth from it (Jaimini 1.2.13, 1.2.69).

In horā, the planets carry the three qualities: Moon, Sun and Jupiter sattva; Mercury and Venus rajas; Mars and Saturn tamas (BJ 2.7); a sāttvika, rājasa or tāmasa person is recognized by his conduct (BS 68.8–9).

The Sun among the grahas: the self (ātman) of Kālapuruṣa and a king (BJ 2.1); male, kṣatriya, sattva, of pitta constitution (BJ 2.6–8); rules Leo, exalted in Aries 10°; Viṃśottarī period 6 years (BPHS 46.15); the avatāra Rāma is born from him (BPHS 2.5); lord of the planets (BPHS 1.6).

The Moon among the grahas: the mind (manas) of Kālapuruṣa and a king (BJ 2.1); female, vaiśya, sattva, of vāta–kapha constitution (BJ 2.6–8); rules Cancer, exalted in Taurus 3°; period 10 years; Kṛṣṇa is born from him (BPHS 2.5); the natal Moon is the base for transits (BS 103).

Mars: strength (sattva) of Kālapuruṣa and the general (BJ 2.1); male, kṣatriya, tamas; lord of fire (BJ 2.6–7); rules Aries and Scorpio, exalted in Capricorn 28°; period 7 years; Narasiṃha is born from him (BPHS 2.5); his Greek-derived name is Āra (BJ 2.2).

Mercury: speech of Kālapuruṣa and the prince (BJ 2.1); neuter, śūdra, rajas, of mixed constitution; lord of earth (BJ 2.6–9); rules Gemini and Virgo, exalted in Virgo 15°; period 17 years; the Buddha is born from him (BPHS 2.5); Greek-derived name Hemna (BJ 2.2).

Jupiter among the grahas: knowledge and happiness of Kālapuruṣa, a minister (BJ 2.1); brahmin, sattva, lord of ether (BJ 2.6–7); rules Sagittarius and Pisces, exalted in Cancer 5°; period 16 years; Vāmana is born from him (BPHS 2.5); his heliacal risings name the years of the sixty-year cycle (BS 8).

Venus: desire (madana) of Kālapuruṣa, a minister honoured by the dānavas (BJ 2.1); female, brahmin, rajas, lord of water (BJ 2.6–7); rules Taurus and Libra, exalted in Pisces 27°; period 20 years; Paraśurāma is born from him (BPHS 2.5); Greek-derived name Āsphujit (BJ 2.3).

Saturn: sorrow (duḥkha) of Kālapuruṣa and the servant (BJ 2.1); neuter, of the lowest class, tamas, lord of air (BJ 2.6–7); rules Capricorn and Aquarius, exalted in Libra 20°; period 19 years; the Tortoise is born from him (BPHS 2.5); aspect of Saturn on the birth-lord gives initiation (BJ 15.3); Greek-derived name Koṇa (BJ 2.2).

The ascending node counted as a planet: in the epic the asura whose severed head, made immortal by the nectar, swallows sun and moon (MBh 1.17); in the siddhāntas the node (pāta) that deflects the moon (SS 2.6); for Varāhamihira not the cause of eclipses but present at them by Brahmā's boon to receive the offerings (BS 5.13–15); the Boar is born from him (BPHS 2.6); period 18 years.

(1) The descending node, the headless trunk of the asura, counted as the ninth graha (BJ 2.3 'Śikhin'); the Fish avatāra is born from him (BPHS 2.6); period 7 years; in the twelfth from the kārakāṃśa he gives kaivalya (Jaimini 1.2.69). (2) A comet (the Ketus of BS 11).
The 'shadow planets' Rāhu and Ketu, without bodies of light, counted with the seven as the nine grahas.

Secondary points treated as minor planets — Dhūma, Vyatīpāta, Pariveṣa, Indracāpa and Upaketu computed from the sun, and Gulika/Māndi and others from the divisions of the day — whose placement is judged with the planets (BPHS 25).
The upagraha 'son of Saturn' computed from the portion of the day or night ruled by Saturn; much used in Kerala horā; Rudra's Kerala commentary finds it encoded in BJ 1.3.

The first sign (Aries), 30° of the zodiac made of nine asterism-quarters; the head of Kālapuruṣa (BJ 1.4); ruled by Mars; movable; of the fire triplicity (later texts); odd, male and cruel (BJ 1.11); Varāhamihira's alternative (Greek-derived) name: kriya (BJ 1.8); dignities: Sun exalted (10°); Saturn in fall (BJ 1.13).

The second sign (Taurus), 30° of the zodiac made of nine asterism-quarters; the face of Kālapuruṣa (BJ 1.4); ruled by Venus; fixed; of the earth triplicity (later texts); even, female and gentle (BJ 1.11); Varāhamihira's alternative (Greek-derived) name: tāvuri (BJ 1.8); dignities: Moon exalted (3°) (BJ 1.13).

The third sign (Gemini), 30° of the zodiac made of nine asterism-quarters; the chest of Kālapuruṣa (BJ 1.4); ruled by Mercury; dual; of the air triplicity (later texts); odd, male and cruel (BJ 1.11); Varāhamihira's alternative (Greek-derived) name: jituma (BJ 1.8); dignities: — (BJ 1.13).

The fourth sign (Cancer), 30° of the zodiac made of nine asterism-quarters; the heart of Kālapuruṣa (BJ 1.4); ruled by the Moon; movable; of the water triplicity (later texts); even, female and gentle (BJ 1.11); Varāhamihira's alternative (Greek-derived) name: kulīra (BJ 1.8); dignities: Jupiter exalted (5°); Mars in fall (BJ 1.13).

The fifth sign (Leo), 30° of the zodiac made of nine asterism-quarters; the belly of Kālapuruṣa (BJ 1.4); ruled by the Sun; fixed; of the fire triplicity (later texts); odd, male and cruel (BJ 1.11); Varāhamihira's alternative (Greek-derived) name: leya (BJ 1.8); dignities: — (BJ 1.13).

The sixth sign (Virgo), 30° of the zodiac made of nine asterism-quarters; the waist of Kālapuruṣa (BJ 1.4); ruled by Mercury; dual; of the earth triplicity (later texts); even, female and gentle (BJ 1.11); Varāhamihira's alternative (Greek-derived) name: pāthona (BJ 1.8); dignities: Mercury exalted (15°); Venus in fall (BJ 1.13).

The seventh sign (Libra), 30° of the zodiac made of nine asterism-quarters; the bladder (lower belly) of Kālapuruṣa (BJ 1.4); ruled by Venus; movable; of the air triplicity (later texts); odd, male and cruel (BJ 1.11); Varāhamihira's alternative (Greek-derived) name: jūka (BJ 1.8); dignities: Saturn exalted (20°); Sun in fall (BJ 1.13).

The eighth sign (Scorpio), 30° of the zodiac made of nine asterism-quarters; the genitals of Kālapuruṣa (BJ 1.4); ruled by Mars; fixed; of the water triplicity (later texts); even, female and gentle (BJ 1.11); Varāhamihira's alternative (Greek-derived) name: kaurpya (BJ 1.8); dignities: Moon in fall (BJ 1.13).

The ninth sign (Sagittarius), 30° of the zodiac made of nine asterism-quarters; the thighs of Kālapuruṣa (BJ 1.4); ruled by Jupiter; dual; of the fire triplicity (later texts); odd, male and cruel (BJ 1.11); Varāhamihira's alternative (Greek-derived) name: taukṣika (BJ 1.8); dignities: — (BJ 1.13).

The tenth sign (Capricorn), 30° of the zodiac made of nine asterism-quarters; the knees of Kālapuruṣa (BJ 1.4); ruled by Saturn; movable; of the earth triplicity (later texts); even, female and gentle (BJ 1.11); Varāhamihira's alternative (Greek-derived) name: ākokera (BJ 1.8); dignities: Mars exalted (28°); Jupiter in fall (BJ 1.13).

The eleventh sign (Aquarius), 30° of the zodiac made of nine asterism-quarters; the shanks of Kālapuruṣa (BJ 1.4); ruled by Saturn; fixed; of the air triplicity (later texts); odd, male and cruel (BJ 1.11); Varāhamihira's alternative (Greek-derived) name: hṛdroga (BJ 1.8); dignities: — (BJ 1.13).

The twelfth sign (Pisces), 30° of the zodiac made of nine asterism-quarters; the feet of Kālapuruṣa (BJ 1.4); ruled by Jupiter; dual; of the water triplicity (later texts); even, female and gentle (BJ 1.11); Varāhamihira's alternative (Greek-derived) name: ittha (BJ 1.8); dignities: Venus exalted (27°); Mercury in fall (BJ 1.13).

Lunar mansion aśvinī: presiding deity the Aśvins (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Ketu (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class swift (kṣipra) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9). Vedic Aśvayujau; first in the later lists, 26th in the Vedāṅga Jyotiṣa's list from Kṛttikā.

notes: Vedic alternative names from memory where given.

definitions.definition: Lunar mansion bharaṇī: presiding deity Yama (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Venus (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class fierce (ugra) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9). Vedic Apabharaṇī; last in the Vedāṅga Jyotiṣa list.

notes: Vedic alternative names from memory where given.

definitions.definition: Lunar mansion kṛttikā: presiding deity Agni (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord the Sun (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class mixed (miśra) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9). First in the Vedic lists (VJ r.25; ŚB 2.1.2.3 on laying the fires under the Kṛttikās).

notes: Vedic alternative names from memory where given.

definitions.definition: Lunar mansion rohiṇī: presiding deity Prajāpati (Brahmā) (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord the Moon (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class fixed (dhruva) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9). The Moon's favourite wife in the Purāṇas.
Lunar mansion mṛgaśiras: presiding deity Soma (the Moon) (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Mars (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class soft (mṛdu) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9).
Lunar mansion ārdrā: presiding deity Rudra (Śiva) (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Rāhu (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class sharp (tīkṣṇa) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9).
Lunar mansion punarvasu: presiding deity Aditi (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Jupiter (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class movable (cara) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9).
Lunar mansion puṣya: presiding deity Bṛhaspati (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Saturn (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class swift (kṣipra) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9). Vedic Tiṣya.

notes: Vedic alternative names from memory where given.

definitions.definition: Lunar mansion āśleṣā: presiding deity the Serpents (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Mercury (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class sharp (tīkṣṇa) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9). Its junction with Maghā is a gaṇḍānta.
Lunar mansion maghā: presiding deity the Fathers (pitṛ) (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Ketu (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class fierce (ugra) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9).
Lunar mansion pūrva-phalgunī: presiding deity Bhaga (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Venus (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class fierce (ugra) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9).
Lunar mansion uttara-phalgunī: presiding deity Aryaman (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord the Sun (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class fixed (dhruva) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9).
Lunar mansion hasta: presiding deity Savitṛ (the Sun) (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord the Moon (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class swift (kṣipra) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9).

Lunar mansion citrā: presiding deity Tvaṣṭṛ (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Mars (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class soft (mṛdu) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9). The star Citrā marks the start of Libra in the Citrāpakṣa ayanāṃśa.

Lunar mansion svātī: presiding deity Vāyu (Wind) (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Rāhu (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class movable (cara) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9). Vedic Niṣṭyā (low confidence).

notes: Vedic alternative names from memory where given.

definitions.definition: Lunar mansion viśākhā: presiding deity Indra-and-Agni (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Jupiter (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class mixed (miśra) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9).
Lunar mansion anurādhā: presiding deity Mitra (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Saturn (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class soft (mṛdu) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9).

Lunar mansion jyeṣṭhā: presiding deity Indra (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Mercury (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class sharp (tīkṣṇa) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9). Its junction with Mūla is a gaṇḍānta (BPHS 94).

Lunar mansion mūla: presiding deity Nirṛti (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Ketu (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class sharp (tīkṣṇa) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9). Birth in Mūla requires pacification (BPHS 93).
Lunar mansion pūrvāṣāḍhā: presiding deity the Waters (āpas) (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Venus (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class fierce (ugra) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9).
Lunar mansion uttarāṣāḍhā: presiding deity the All-gods (viśvedevāḥ) (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord the Sun (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class fixed (dhruva) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9).

Lunar mansion abhijit: presiding deity Brahmā (Vidhi) (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord — (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class swift (kṣipra) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9). 28th asterism, used in muhūrta (MC 2.1, 2.6) but absent from the Vedāṅga Jyotiṣa list and from the Viṃśottarī scheme.

Lunar mansion śravaṇa: presiding deity Viṣṇu (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord the Moon (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class movable (cara) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9). Vedic Śroṇā (moderate confidence).

notes: Vedic alternative names from memory where given.

definitions.definition: Lunar mansion dhaniṣṭhā: presiding deity the Vasus (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Mars (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class movable (cara) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9). Vedic Śraviṣṭhā, at whose beginning the Vedāṅga Jyotiṣa places the northward turning (VJ r.6); with Jupiter's rising here the sixty-year cycle begins (BS 8.27).

notes: Vedic alternative names from memory where given.

definitions.definition: Lunar mansion śatabhiṣaj: presiding deity Varuṇa (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Rāhu (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class movable (cara) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9).

Lunar mansion pūrva-bhādrapadā: presiding deity Aja Ekapād (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Jupiter (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class fierce (ugra) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9). Vedic Proṣṭhapadā.

notes: Vedic alternative names from memory where given.

definitions.definition: Lunar mansion uttara-bhādrapadā: presiding deity Ahirbudhnya (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Saturn (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class fixed (dhruva) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9).

Lunar mansion revatī: presiding deity Pūṣan (VJ r.25–27; BS 97.4–5; MC 2.1); Viṃśottarī period-lord Mercury (BPHS 46.12); muhūrta class soft (mṛdu) (MC 2.2–8; BS 97.6–9). Its junction with Aśvinī is a gaṇḍānta.
